answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with recurring proof-of-work upkeep: every identity must solve a fresh cipher puzzle each epoch to stay active, and difficulty rises toward a summit set by total network load. Each solved puzzle joins a river of ongoing proofs — cheap for one honest agent, but an attacker running a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand puzzles of compute every epoch, forever. Identities that stop proving work are dropped automatically, so a Sybil swarm cannot rest: its cost is continuous, while honest agents pay only one puzzle each.
